title: Varaha
hook: the earth has sunk to the bottom, and a boar dives in
tomorrow: why would a god lift the earth like someone he loves?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Kurma, and the taste the whole churning was for: Mohini pouring, and one sip Rahu couldn't give back. Kurma's run is done. The earth itself sinks into the sea. Who goes down for it?

When someone you love has a bad week, it's tempting to call down from the top of the stairs: you okay? The third descent doesn't do that. The earth has sunk to the bottom of the cosmic waters, and nothing can live on her. Brahma is wondering how to raise her. And then, out of Brahma's own nostril, comes a boar.
screen: `YOU OKAY? FROM THE TOP OF THE STAIRS.` → `THE EARTH HAS SUNK.` → `A BOAR APPEARS.`

segments.voice: In the Bhagavata Purana's telling, the boar is tiny at first, the size of a thumb, and in moments grows as large as an elephant, then larger still. That's Varaha, Vishnu's third descent. He roars, plunges into the waters, and goes all the way down, searching through the deep to where the earth lies. He lifts her on his tusks and carries her up. In the Vishnu Purana, the earth herself speaks as he comes for her, and praises him. In the Bhagavata, a demon named Hiranyaksha meets Varaha on the way up; that fight comes later in the run. Now look at the shape of this help. Varaha doesn't send for the earth or wait for her to float up. He goes down to where she is, all the way, into the dark water, and lifts from below. Help that gets wet. This week, it might be a friend after bad news, a brother who won't leave his room, a parent having a hard month. The story's picture isn't advice called from the shore. It's a boar in the deep, and a tusk under the weight.
screen: `A THUMB-SIZED BOAR GROWS.` · `ALL THE WAY DOWN.` · `LIFTED ON HIS TUSKS.` · then, large: `HELP THAT GETS WET.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one person who seems sunk right now. Silently name what you wish for them; then what makes it hard to reach them; then one plain way to go to where they are, a knock, a walk, a message. Give each of the three a few slow breaths. If you pray, you can hold them before God.
Varaha: the boar, Vishnu's third descent, who dives to the bottom of the waters and lifts the earth.
Your line: Varaha. Down to where it sank, then up with it on his tusks. See you tomorrow.
